w: Founded in 1885, this is the oldest art museum in the western United States. Its collection spans American work from the Gold Rush era to today, European paintings and master drawings, and one of the country's largest international ceramics holdings, plus Asian, African and Oceanic art.
s: Oldest art museum in the American West, since 1885
_facts: Founded 1885, the oldest art museum in the Western US
Holds American art from the Gold Rush era to the present
One of the largest international ceramics collections in the US
Accredited by the American Alliance of Museums

w: A vertical-lift bridge across the Sacramento River, once known as the M Street Bridge and carrying US Route 40 and US Route 99W. Now maintained by Caltrans as State Route 275, it links West Sacramento's West Capitol Avenue to the Capitol Mall. Added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1982.
s: Vertical-lift bridge over the Sacramento River
_facts: Vertical-lift bridge over the Sacramento River
Formerly known as the M Street Bridge
Once carried US Route 40 and US Route 99W
Added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1982

n: Leland Stanford Mansion State Historic Park
w: Built in 1856 as the home of Leland Stanford, California's 8th governor and founder of Stanford University. The family donated it in 1900 to the Catholic Diocese of Sacramento, which ran a children's home there until 1978, before the state bought it as the governor's ceremonial reception center.
s: Leland Stanford's 1856 mansion, now a state park
_facts: Built 1856 for Leland Stanford, California's 8th governor
Stanford also founded Stanford University
Ran as a Catholic children's home from 1900 to 1978
Now the state's official ceremonial reception center

w: Downtown at 11th and K Streets, this is the mother church of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Sacramento and one of the largest cathedrals west of the Mississippi. The diocese serves around a million Catholics. Its size made it the venue for former governors' funeral Masses, most recently Pat Brown's in 1996.
s: One of the largest cathedrals west of the Mississippi
_facts: Mother church of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Sacramento
One of the largest cathedrals west of the Mississippi River
Diocese serves about 1,000,000 Catholics across 102 churches
Hosted Governor Pat Brown's funeral Mass in 1996

w: Housed in Old Sacramento State Historic Park at 111 I Street, this museum is run by the California State Parks system. Its exhibits interpret the role that railroads played in shaping the development of the Western United States, from construction through operation.
s: Railroad history museum in Old Sacramento
_facts: Run by the California State Parks system
Located in Old Sacramento State Historic Park, at 111 I Street
Interprets the role of railroads in the Western United States

w: California's state history museum, one block from the Capitol at 1020 O Street inside the March Fong Eu Secretary of State Building. Formerly called the Golden State Museum, it is a private nonprofit run in partnership with the state, and houses both the California Hall of Fame and the Unity Center.
s: State history museum steps from the Capitol
_facts: California's official state history museum
One block from the State Capitol, inside the March Fong Eu building
Home to the California Hall of Fame and the Unity Center
Formerly known as the Golden State Museum

w: Opened in William Land Park on June 2, 1927, with just 40 animals across 4.2 acres. An early-1960s expansion grew the grounds to 14.3 acres, and by December 2012 the zoo held just over 500 animals.
s: A 1927 zoo tucked inside William Land Park
